Optimal.Notes: Setting the refresh rate to 40 Hz and capping to 40 fps delivers a smooth, tear-free experience that looks great with FSR upscaling from 1024x640. This is the recommended sweet spot for most players on the LCD Deck.

profiles.Summary: God of War runs well on the Steam Deck, achieving a stable 40 fps at medium-to-low settings with FSR upscaling — the game's PC minimum spec (GTX 960) is close to the Deck's GPU class, making it a solid fit. With tuning, the experience is cinematic and smooth, though demanding areas like large open spaces can stress the GPU.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated by comparing the game's PC minimum GPU requirement (GTX 960 / R9 290X) against the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class). On first run, check the frame pacing in the opening area and in Midgard's larger spaces — if you see consistent dips below target, drop to the Max Battery profile or reduce Shadow Quality first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Aggressive TDP and GPU clock limits with a low render resolution and FSR stretch the battery significantly. The 30 fps cap keeps power draw consistent and prevents thermal throttle spikes.

KnownIssues: Shader compilation stutters can occur early in the game on first run; these diminish after the first hour of play.
Some cutscene transitions may exhibit brief frame dips in GPU-heavy environments.
No Deck-specific player reports found; profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware comparison.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapped TDP lets the APU boost fully, but expect frame rate variance between 45 and 60 fps in demanding outdoor scenes; consider dropping to 45 fps cap if stutters are noticeable. Battery life will be short.

Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz gives the smoothest feel on the OLED panel with minimal tearing; rendering at 1024x640 with Deck FSR produces a clean 1280x800 image. Medium textures and shadows look noticeably better than Low without pushing the GPU past its limits.

profiles.Summary: God of War runs well on the Steam Deck OLED, achieving a stable 40 fps at medium-to-low settings with FSR upscaling — the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU sits comfortably between the minimum and recommended PC specs. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, and ProtonDB reports a strong platinum rating, indicating a smooth out-of-the-box experience under Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports or guides were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs relative to Deck GPU capability (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class, between the minimum GTX 960 and recommended GTX 1060). On your first run, check frame pacing in the opening combat encounter and the Lake of Nine overworld — if the Optimal profile dips below 35 fps consistently, drop to Max Battery settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 and upscaling via Deck FSR keeps GPU load low; the 9 W TDP and 900 MHz GPU clock lock further reduce heat and power draw. Motion Blur and Film Grain are disabled to keep the low-res FSR image as clean as possible.

KnownIssues: Some users report occasional shader compilation stutters early in the game that subside after the first hour of play.
The game's default resolution scaling can conflict with Deck FSR; setting in-game resolution to native before applying Deck-level FSR is recommended.
High-quality shadow and texture settings can cause frame dips in dense combat encounters on the Deck GPU.
No native Linux build — runs via Proton, but platinum ProtonDB tier means compatibility is excellent with minimal issues.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full 15 W TDP and native 1280x800, the Deck can reach 60 fps in simpler areas but will dip to 45-50 fps in heavy combat or dense environments — consider dropping the cap to 45 if dips are bothersome. Battery life is short at this setting; keep a charger nearby.
